title: The drugstore at 12th and Central
summary: Howard and Collette recall the drugstore below 12th and Central where musicians met evenings and found work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Marshall Royal mentioned something about a drugstore at 12th and Central where there were an awful lot of musicians around. But that was probably a little later.
Possibly.
Well, I don't know why Marshall couldn't tell you any more about it, 'cause he was younger. I was older, and had a start on him.
Well, that's right. That's why we're here. We wanta' get information that was before Marshall could tell us anything.
Well, didn't he tell you something?
He told us some things, but there's some things he doesn't know because he wasn't there that early.
No, he wad'n't.
Do you remember the drugstore at 12th and Central?
Sure.
Well, what was it?
What was it?
Yeah. Was that where musicians would hang out?
Yeah, that's where they'd hang out.
What'd they call it, do you remember?
Huh?
Did they have a name for the drugstore?
Drugstore had a name; it had a name--
12th Street?
--Can't tell you a name--
Uh-huh.
It'll come to me after a while.
So did they hang out during the day there, or night only--you know, or just all the time? Musicians?
They'd come down there in the evenings.
Yeah. And sort of meet each other--
Yeah.
--and get work, and sort of talk.
Talk, you know.
Was it a good place for food and everything, too?
Yeah, good place for food.
Uh-huh.
And the man who owned it, see, I got to remember who he is. Give me a chance, gentlemen, will you?
Okay.
I--I can't remember all them things. Go 'way back, a hundred years. (laughter)
It seems like that, doesn't it?
It seems that way.
Yeah, but as long as we know there was a spot like that, where the musicians would meet.
That's where they met.
12th and Central was about it?
12th and Central? No. It was down below 12th and Central.
Below 12th and Central?
Lemme' see. Can't think what the man's name was that run the place. He was a good guy, fine fellow, too.
Uh-huh.
Can't think of his name.
So, at that period, can I ask this question, then? Was that like the main section of Central, then? You know, naturally before--
Yeah.
--the forties, when the Alabam and all that--you know, 'cause later on, as I was going up--
Oh, yeah, before the forties--
--I heard that 12th--huh?
You were just coming by ; you were just gettin'--
Yeah, but I heard that the 12th Street and around in there was really the spot at that time.
It was.
Yeah. Okay.
